SOFTER — two levels

Same layout, same fonts, saturation pulled down. The old versions are still on page 3 if you want to compare.

MUTED — periwinkle instead of electric blue, soft coral instead of hot coral, butter instead of acid lime. Keeps a small offset shadow on the primary button, but tinted rather than black. Still recognisably the same family, just quieter.

PASTEL — softest. No outlines at all, blurred shadows, bigger radii, colour only as gentle washes. Calm and premium; less of the print-poster energy.

WHICH WAY TO LEAN

Muted still has a bit of edge — the flat shapes and the small offset shadow keep some character, so it won't read as generic.

Pastel is genuinely gentle, but it's also where most soft SaaS design lands. It risks being forgettable, which was the original complaint about looking like everyone else.

If you want softer still but not anonymous, say "Muted, but drop the offset shadow" — that's the midpoint and takes a minute.

ONE REAL FIX, NOT JUST TASTE

In the first draft the Spanish sentences were coral text on white — roughly 3:1 contrast, under the readable floor for body copy. Fine for a mockup, bad for a reading app.

Both soft versions now separate the two languages with a soft background tint and keep both texts in ink. Softer to look at and actually legible — which is the same change either way you go.

THE MUTED SYSTEM APPLIED

Your real screens, real content — the demo story "The Last Minute" (B1, Football, English→Spanish) from the app's own data.

English sits on a periwinkle tint, Spanish on a coral tint, consistently across reader, landing preview and quiz. That's the --lang-primary-tint / --lang-secondary-tint pair already sitting unused in globals.css, finally doing something.

READER — the hide/show mechanic

Third row shows the hidden state. Today it's opacity-0, which leaves an invisible-but-present block. Here it's a dashed placeholder, so it reads as "deliberately concealed, tap to reveal" rather than "broken".

That's a behaviour change, not just colour — say if you'd rather keep the current invisible treatment.

THE FIRST DRAFT — kept for comparison

These are the two tunings from before you asked for softer: electric blue, hot coral, acid lime, with 1.5px and 2px ink outlines.

Nothing here is live. Page 1 is where the decision is.
